<b>Латеральная прямая мышца</b> идёт от: The lateral rectus runs from the common ring along the lateral wall of the orbit and inserts into the sclera 7 mm from the edge of the cornea. Its only action is to abduct the eye toward the temple. Nerve: the abducens (VI); when it is damaged, the eye cannot turn outward and drifts toward the nose.
<b>Медиальная прямая</b> — самая сильная: The medial rectus is the strongest of the rectus muscles. It runs along the medial wall and inserts closest to the cornea (5.5 mm). It adducts the eye toward the nose and, together with the muscle of the other eye, turns both eyes inward for near vision. Nerve: inferior branch of the oculomotor (III).
<b>Верхняя прямая</b> лежит под мышцей,: The superior rectus lies under the levator of the eyelid. The axis of the orbit is about 23° off the line of sight, so the muscle not only elevates the eye but also turns its upper pole toward the nose and adducts it. It elevates most purely when the eye is turned toward the temple. Nerve: superior branch of III.
<b>Нижняя прямая</b> лежит над дном глаз: The inferior rectus lies above the orbital floor. It depresses the eye and, because of its oblique course, also turns its upper pole toward the temple and adducts it. It depresses most purely when the eye is turned toward the temple. Nerve: inferior branch of III.
<b>Верхняя косая</b> идёт от вершины гла: The superior oblique runs from the apex of the orbit forward to the trochlea, a cartilage loop at the upper inner rim. There its tendon turns back and outward, passes under the superior rectus, and inserts behind the equator. It depresses, intorts, and abducts the eye; it is the key muscle for looking down and in. Nerve: trochlear (IV).
<b>Нижняя косая</b> — единственная мышца: The inferior oblique is the only eye muscle that starts in front: on the orbital floor next to the lacrimal fossa. It runs back and outward under the inferior rectus and inserts on the back outer part of the eye. It elevates, extorts, and abducts the eye; it is the key muscle for looking up and in. Nerve: III.
<b>Мышца, поднимающая верхнее веко,</b>: The levator palpebrae superioris lies above the superior rectus and becomes a broad tendon woven into the upper lid. Nerve: III. Attached to it is Müller's smooth muscle with sympathetic supply, which is why in Horner syndrome the lid droops by only 1–2 mm.
<b>Вверх и влево.</b> Правый глаз привед: Up and left. The right eye is turned toward the nose. In this position the axis of the inferior oblique is closest to the line of sight, and it does almost all the lifting — this is how the inferior oblique is tested.
<b>Взгляд вверх</b> — вместе работают ве: Looking up uses the superior rectus and the inferior oblique together. One rotates the eye inward, the other outward, so the rotations cancel, and so do their side pulls. The upper lid rises along with the eye.
<b>Вверх и вправо.</b> Правый глаз отвед: Up and right. The right eye is turned toward the temple, and the axis of the superior rectus lines up with the line of sight — it does almost all the lifting. This is how the superior rectus is tested.
<b>Взгляд влево.</b> Правый глаз приводи: Looking left. The right eye is pulled toward the nose by the medial rectus (III) while the lateral rectus relaxes: antagonist muscles work as a pair. The left eye turns outward at the same time — the eyes move together.
<b>Взгляд прямо.</b> Все мышцы слегка на: Looking straight ahead. All the muscles are slightly tense and balance each other. In six positions — right, left, and the four diagonals — the eye is moved mainly by a single muscle: by having you trace an “H” with your gaze, a doctor tests each one separately.
<b>Взгляд вправо.</b> Правый глаз отводи: Looking right. The right eye turns toward the temple — the lateral rectus (VI) is working. Meanwhile the left eye turns toward the nose with its medial rectus: a gaze center in the brainstem sends the command to both eyes.
<b>Вниз и влево.</b> В приведённом глазу: Down and left. In the adducted eye, almost all of the downward pull comes from the superior oblique. This is how we look when reading or walking downstairs — which is why trochlear nerve (IV) palsy makes going down stairs hard.
<b>Взгляд вниз</b> — нижняя прямая и вер: Looking down uses the inferior rectus and the superior oblique. Their rotations are opposite and cancel out. The upper lid lowers along with the eye, so no white shows above the iris.
<b>Вниз и вправо.</b> В отведённом глазу: Down and right. In the abducted eye, the axis of the inferior rectus lines up with the line of sight — it does almost all the lowering. This is how the inferior rectus is tested.
<b>Зрительный нерв (II)</b> — пучок ≈ 1,: The optic nerve (II) is a bundle of about 1.2 million axons of retinal cells. It leaves the orbit through the optic canal together with the ophthalmic artery. Inside the orbit the nerve is longer than the distance to the canal and lies in an S-curve — slack that lets the eye turn. Its further path is in the “Vision” topic.
<b>Глазодвигательный нерв (III)</b> вход: The oculomotor nerve (III) enters through the superior orbital fissure inside the common ring. Its superior branch goes to the superior rectus and the lid levator, the inferior branch to the medial and inferior recti and the inferior oblique. From the inferior branch, fibers run to the ciliary ganglion to constrict the pupil and focus the lens.
<b>Паралич III нерва.</b> Работают тольк: Oculomotor (III) palsy. Only the lateral rectus (VI) and superior oblique (IV) still work, so the eye is turned down and out. The lid droops (ptosis), and the pupil is wide and does not constrict to light. If an aneurysm compresses the nerve, the pupil widens first — a reason for emergency care.
<b>Блоковый нерв (IV)</b> — самый тонкий: The trochlear nerve (IV) is the thinnest cranial nerve and the only one that leaves the back of the brainstem. It enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure above the common ring, passes over the lid levator, and enters the superior oblique muscle.
<b>Паралич IV нерва.</b> Без верхней кос: Trochlear (IV) palsy. Without the superior oblique, the eye sits slightly higher than the other and its upper pole is tilted toward the temple. Vertical double vision is worse when looking down and in — reading and on stairs. To get rid of it, the person tilts the head toward the healthy shoulder.
<b>Отводящий нерв (VI)</b> проходит чере: The abducens nerve (VI) passes through the common ring and enters the inner surface of the lateral rectus. It has the longest course inside the skull, so it is often affected when intracranial pressure rises.
<b>Паралич VI нерва.</b> Латеральная пря: Abducens (VI) palsy. The lateral rectus does not work and the medial rectus pulls unopposed — the eye turns toward the nose and cannot move toward the temple. Double vision is horizontal and worse when looking into the distance and toward the affected side.
<b>Глазной нерв (V₁)</b> — чувствительна: The ophthalmic nerve (V₁) is a sensory branch of the trigeminal. Before the fissure it divides into the lacrimal, frontal, and nasociliary nerves, which carry sensation from the eye, cornea, lids, forehead, and nose. Along the orbital floor runs the infraorbital nerve (V₂) to the cheek. Corneal reflex: touching the cornea (V₁) → a blink (VII).
<b>Слёзная железа</b> — размером с минда: The lacrimal gland is about the size of an almond. The tendon of the lid levator divides it into orbital and palpebral parts; 6–12 ducts open into the upper conjunctival fornix. Its secretory fibers are parasympathetic, from the facial nerve via the pterygopalatine ganglion: damage to the nerve near the brainstem leaves the eye dry.
<b>Слёзные точки и канальцы.</b> На внут: Lacrimal puncta and canaliculi. At the inner end of each lid, on a small papilla, is a punctum about 0.3 mm across, facing the eye. From it a canaliculus runs 2 mm vertically, then about 8 mm toward the nose; usually the two join into a common canaliculus. Most tears drain through the lower one.
<b>Слёзный мешок</b> (12–15 мм) лежит в: The lacrimal sac (12–15 mm) lies in a fossa on the medial wall of the orbit. With each blink the orbicularis oculi stretches and squeezes it in turn, like a pump. The nasolacrimal duct (12–18 mm) opens into the inferior nasal meatus under the inferior concha — which is why your nose runs when you cry.
<b>Веки.</b> Основа века — плотная пласт: Eyelids. Each lid is built on a dense plate (the tarsus). It holds about 30 glands in the upper lid and 20 in the lower: their oil forms the outer layer of the tear film and keeps it from evaporating. The orbicularis oculi (VII) closes the lids; the levator (III) raises the upper one. We blink 15–20 times a minute.
<b>Глазница</b> — костная пирамида глуби: The orbit is a bony pyramid 4.5–5 cm deep with its apex pointing back. At the apex, the four rectus muscles arise from the common tendinous ring; the obliques reach the eye from above and below. Pick a muscle or a gaze direction: the arrows show where the person is looking, from their own point of view.
<b>Нервы глазницы.</b> Через зрительный: Nerves of the orbit. The optic nerve passes through the optic canal; the nerves of the eye muscles (III, IV, VI) and the ophthalmic nerve (V₁) pass through the superior orbital fissure. Muscles are colored by nerve: III orange, IV green, VI blue. Pick a nerve; for III, IV, and VI you can turn on “Palsy.”
<b>Слёзный аппарат.</b> Слёзы выделяет ж: The lacrimal apparatus. Tears are made by a gland in the upper outer corner of the orbit. Blinking spreads them over the eye and sweeps them to the inner corner, into the lacrimal lake. From there they drain through the puncta and canaliculi into the lacrimal sac, and down the nasolacrimal duct into the nose.
Шесть мышц поворачивают глаз так точно,: Six muscles turn the eye so precisely that both eyes always point at the same spot. Three nerves control them, while tears constantly wash the eye and drain into the nose. See which muscle works for each direction of gaze and what happens when a nerve is paralyzed.
\n <div><h2>Устройство</h2>\n:
Structure

The orbit is a four-sided pyramid made of seven bones: frontal, sphenoid, ethmoid, lacrimal, zygomatic, maxilla, and palatine. The medial walls of the two orbits are parallel, while their axes diverge at about 45°. The orbit holds about 30 mL, and the eye fills only a fifth of that; the rest is muscles, the fat body, vessels, and nerves.

The rectus muscles arise from the common tendinous ring around the optic canal; the obliques reach the eye from the front and below and (via the trochlea) from the front and above, and insert behind the equator. The optics of the eye and the visual pathway are covered in the “Vision” topic.

How it works

The eyes move together: a gaze center in the brainstem sends a single command to muscles of both eyes, for example the lateral rectus of the right eye and the medial rectus of the left. The image falls on matching spots of the two retinas, and we see one object, not two.

The tear film, a few micrometers thick, has three layers: mucus from conjunctival cells, a watery layer from the lacrimal gland, and oil from the lid glands. It nourishes the cornea, washes away dust, and kills microbes with the enzyme lysozyme.

Medicine

  • Strabismus — the axes of the eyes do not line up. In children the brain suppresses the image from the deviating eye, and without treatment a “lazy eye” (amblyopia) develops.
  • Double vision (diplopia) — a common first sign of a III, IV, or VI nerve palsy: in diabetes, a tumor, an aneurysm, or raised intracranial pressure.
  • Orbital floor fracture from a blow to the eye: the inferior rectus gets trapped in the crack, the eye cannot look up, and the cheek goes numb (infraorbital nerve).
  • Horner syndrome — damage to the sympathetic pathway: mild ptosis, a small pupil, and dry facial skin on the same side.
  • Dry eye and dacryocystitis — too few tears, and inflammation of the lacrimal sac when the nasolacrimal duct is blocked (in infants the duct often opens late).

Simplifications

  • The skull scan is translucent, and the orbital walls over the muscles are cut away depending on the view; the fat body, fasciae, conjunctiva, vessels, and the contents of the left orbit (except the eye and lids) are not shown.
  • Muscles are bands on straight paths that wrap around the eye; insertion sites, thickness, and bulging during contraction are averages. The eye turns without rotating around the line of sight.
  • The lids are a shell around the palpebral fissure without layers; the tarsal plates, their glands, and the orbicularis oculi are not shown. Nerves are drawn schematically, the arteries and veins of the orbit are not shown, and tear flow is sped up.
